result.strongest_objection: Two mutants (`MUT-PENDING-AS-FOREIGN` and `MUT-CONTROL-ANY-ACCEPT`) survive the mutation suite, though the doc explicitly justifies `MUT-PENDING-AS-FOREIGN` as unreachable by construction (1.5s window bound > 500ms read deadline) and `MUT-CONTROL-ANY-ACCEPT` as independently pinned by `TP` and `TC`.

The pinned patch (V13, ci.yml +1/-1) adds only the four Net6 names, so if the premise is false the patch ships with the new s.end(line) tunnel write never measured anywhere: local runs skip real srt (no bwrap, WORLD_EXEC_SRT_NODE_MODULES unset, final UNMEASURED row), and the executor's full go test ./... also skips it. Every other consequential claim in this doc carries a V row; the one that props up the doc's largest UNMEASURED surface does not, and its falsehood would silently void R4's stated mitigation while leaving the byte-exact patch incomplete.
result.catch: Two secondary items to fix in the same revision: (1) the window() bound of 1.5 s is load-bearing — Claim A's pending-to-silent mapping and the MUT-PENDING-AS-FOREIGN row both depend on it — yet it is never stated in §3; it first appears inside the §5 mutation table, so a reader of the design body cannot reconstruct it (§3.5's constants list omits it). (2) 'Unreachable by construction' for MUT-PENDING-AS-FOREIGN is overstated: a dial accepted in the final ~second of an extended window wait can still be pending at the bound (accept taken after W+1000 with a 500 ms deadline past W+1500). The design still fails closed (pending maps to silent) and the survivor is benign, but the stated justification is arithmetically wrong and should be corrected rather than hand-waved.
result.proposed_fix: Add a V16 row: grep -n 'TestExecSrtStartupProbePasses' .github/workflows/ci.yml (or paste ci.yml:247 in full) to $V/designer-greps.txt. If present, cite the exact line in R4. If absent, the patch must append it to the tests= list as a fifth name (ci.yml becomes two added names), with V13's ci.yml sha and numstat re-measured and §8 updated — do not let M1 merge on the current byte-exact patch until this is resolved. Additionally, in §3.3 name the bound as a constant (e.g. execProbeNet6WindowWait = 3 x execProbeNet6Wait = 1.5 s, with its reason: strictly exceeds the classifier deadline so a fully-arrived accept is always classified, and pending-at-bound fails closed as silent), and rewrite MUT-PENDING-AS-FOREIGN's rationale as: reachable only by a dial accepted in the last wait-interval of an already-extended window; the design maps pending to silent and fails closed, and the mutant's delta is confined to late-landing foreign dials (inconclusive-retry instead of fail), which still cannot pass a deterministic dialer because attempt 3 fails per TE — the survivor is benign for its behavior, not because it is unreachable.

result.strongest_objection: Gate 2 failure: the design transplants the reverse leg's exact classification rule (row 230: child/foreign/silent, foreign-retried, silent-sticky, nonce-in-op-arg) yet implements it as a wholly parallel stack — new types `net6Class`, `net6Window`, `net6Leg`, `classifyNet6Dial`, plus mark/window bookkeeping — without one sentence justifying why the reverse leg's existing classifier and bounded-retry machinery in the same file cannot be reused or factored. 'Reuses the vocabulary' is not a reuse analysis. Two nonce-line classifiers with independently chosen constants (500 ms read deadline vs. the reverse leg's deadlines; an unnamed 1.5 s `window()` bound that appears for the first time in the mutation table and is absent from the §3.5 constants list) create a silent-divergence hazard on a fail-closed gate: a future fix to one classifier need not reach the other, and TS/TC pin only the new one. On a reject-by-default rubric, the most-similar existing machinery in the codebase is precisely the thing the doc never analyzes.
result.catch: Ask the author to (a) add a conflict-surface paragraph covering the reverse leg's classifier implementation (not just its semantics): enumerate its entry points, deadlines and retry driver, and justify duplication vs. factoring a shared line-classifier; (b) pin every timing constant — §5's mutant table references a `window()` bound of 1.5 s that §3.5 never lists as a constant (only `execProbeDialPrefix`, `execProbeNet6Wait` 500 ms, `execProbeNet6Attempts` 3) — either name it (`execProbeNet6WindowWait`) with its derivation from the 500 ms read deadline, or correct the mutant-table text; (c) confirm via grep that the reverse leg's deadlines are untouched so the two stacks' parameters are stated side by side, proving divergence is deliberate, not accidental.
result.proposed_fix: Add a new §3.1.1 'Why the reverse leg's machinery is not reused': 'The reverse leg (row 230) classifies one inbound line inside a fixed post-connect handshake with its own read deadline and a leg-scoped retry loop; it holds no notion of multi-accept windows, cumulative ordering across three forward legs, or per-attempt windows. The forward legs need accept-order windows spanning Run A through the proxy leg's last sample, so the window/mark bookkeeping has no reverse-leg analogue. The byte-level decision — exact expected line vs. first-diverging byte vs. EOF/deadline — is, however, identical to the reverse leg's. Factor that into a shared helper `classifyDialLine(conn, want []string, deadline) ` called by both legs; the forward-specific mapping (foreign→window inconclusive→bounded re-run, silent→fail) stays in `net6Leg`, exactly as the reverse leg keeps its own sticky mapping. If factoring is rejected at quorum, record the reverse leg's deadline values here and state that the 500 ms/1.5 s/3-attempt constants were chosen independently, with a grep row proving the reverse leg's parameters are unchanged.' Additionally: add `execProbeNet6WindowWait` (1.5 s, derived as > 2×`execProbeNet6Wait` so no accept can be pending at the bound — the MUT-PENDING-AS-FOREIGN reachability argument depends on it) to the §3.5 constants list, and add verification row V16: `grep -n 'execProbe.*Wait\|Deadline' host/broker/exec_probe.go` showing both legs' constants on one screen, confirming no silent edits to the reverse leg.

controller_in_session.note: Direction sound: per-window HEAD pass condition kept; silent and child fail at once; foreign-only windows retried at most 3. Watch R2 (intermittent byte-altering escape passes 1-p^3 vs HEAD 1-p) and whether the classifier read deadline/pending-accept handling is airtight.
